I am thinking of building a gaming PC somewhere in the neighborhood of $1000 dollars, give or take $200. I'm not sure if this is the right place to ask, and I know that there are literally millions of forums that cover this topic, but there is literally SO MUCH information out there I figured it wouldn't hurt to ask this community.

I'm skilled enough with my hands and confident in my abilities to build a pc from scratch, but my tech knowledge goes as far as knowing a bit about each component and its function. There are so many options out there, and so many opinions that are difficult to discern between without some first-hand knowledge. I don't want to have any regrets my first go 'round in this process, so any and all advice is welcome.

I found a basic $1000 build I figured would make a good starting point, or template, from which to start. In particular I am curious about the addition of an SSD, or any other concerns. I'd like to stay on budget, but I don't mind spending an extra $200 dollars or so to maybe go a bit overboard in some respects, as long as it guarantees performance benefits and/or future adaptability concerns.

I do it step by step, every couple of months I replace something to something better.

But make sure that you get a big enough case first. Something that can be easily opened and modified and can support tons of cooling ventilators.

Second a good enough power supply.

I use this case:

Carbide Series® Air 540 High Airflow ATX Cube Case.
http://www.corsair.com/en/carbide-series-air-540-high-airflow-atx-cube-case

It is big but also theft proof. I don't think that thieves will take this monster.
For a template I normally go through pcpartpicker's builds link for $800-$1200 USD.

750 watt PSU is probably overkill. 16GB of RAM should be somewhere around $60 - no reason to skimp. ATX case and mobo are going to be bigger than mATX. 4690k may be a lot cheaper and is not really that much slower than the 4790k.

Do you really need an optical drive at this point?

This is a bit more expensive, but pretty dang cheap for a 1TB SSD http://www.newegg.com/Product/Product.aspx?Item=N82E16820226596

Combined with pcpartpicker, as others have suggested, I would recommend using Logical Increments. Its pricing information isn't as up-to-date as Pcpartipicker, but it gives you a good overview of part tiers and how they compare to each other.
